missedDefects: Wrong leaving-digit direction after restocking from sold out. In LowStockIndicator.svelte, `dir` is a `$derived.by` that mutates `prevStock` and `lastDir`, and it is only read by `remember` and `flipIn`, which run only while a count is rendered. While the block is sold out no count exists, so `prevStock` keeps the last pre-sell-out value. In the original, `if (safeStock !== prevStock) { setPrevStock(safeStock); setDir(...) }` runs on every render. Repro in the judge's own sequence: `set(1,{stock:1})` then sell to 0 (`sell1`) then back to 1 (`back1`). On the 0 to 1 render the svelte `dir` sees 1 === `prevStock` (1), skips the update and keeps `lastDir` -1 from the earlier 3 to 1 drop. The original sets dir to +1 for that increase. The re-created digit "1" therefore gets `dataset.dir` of "-1" in the port, versus an exit direction of -100% in the original. A following restock 1 to 2 then makes the "1" leave downward (+100%) in svelte but upward (-100%) in the original. This breaks "the leaving digit keeps the direction of the change that created it". The judge's `back1` only checked that no slide happens on re-entry and never ran a further change. The same wrong direction appears when restocking to any value at or below the pre-sell-out stock, for example 7 to 0, then 0 to 1, because it compares 1 against the stale 7 and gets -1 where the original gets +1. Vue is not affected: its `watch(safeStock, ..., { flush: 'sync' })` runs on every change.
